claim_text: Protein requirements for healthy adults are expressed relative to body weight; the reference adult RDA is 0.8 g/kg/day.
applicability: requires body weight and whole-day intake; not a single-dish threshold
uncertainty: requirements may differ by age, activity and clinical state
prohibited_overclaims: this dish meets protein needs; more protein is universally better

claim_text: Increasing daily protein intake can produce small additional gains in lean body mass and some strength outcomes when combined with resistance exercise in healthy adults.
applicability: exercise, age and total daily intake modify effect
uncertainty: physical-function and handgrip effects are limited/unclear
prohibited_overclaims: high-protein dish prevents sarcopenia; protein alone replaces resistance exercise

claim_text: Calcium is required for bone structure and maintenance, and recommended intakes vary by age and sex.
uncertainty: dish contribution cannot be judged without serving/basis
prohibited_overclaims: a calcium-rich dish prevents fractures; supplement evidence equals food evidence

claim_text: Routine calcium and/or vitamin D supplementation was not associated with lower fracture incidence in community-dwelling older adults in a large RCT meta-analysis.
applicability: supplementation context only; does not negate adequacy requirements
prohibited_overclaims: calcium is useless for bone health; dietary calcium has no value

claim_text: Iron requirements vary substantially by sex, pregnancy and dietary bioavailability; nonheme iron is less bioavailable than heme iron.
applicability: requires demographic context and iron-source/bioavailability information
uncertainty: current dish field reports total iron only
prohibited_overclaims: same iron threshold for all adults; total dish iron predicts absorbed iron

claim_text: Routine prenatal iron supplementation reduces iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anemia at term, while evidence for broader maternal and infant clinical outcomes is limited.
applicability: pregnancy supplementation evidence; not a general dish recommendation
uncertainty: clinical outcomes beyond hematologic endpoints remain uncertain
prohibited_overclaims: iron-rich dish substitutes for clinical screening/treatment; universal pregnancy supplementation claim from dish iron

claim_text: Natural food folate, synthetic folic acid and dietary folate equivalents are not interchangeable measurement objects.
applicability: source must identify nutrient form and DFE conversion semantics
uncertainty: current source field FolicAcid is semantically unresolved
prohibited_overclaims: treat FolicAcid μg as DFE; treat dish food folate as proven folic-acid supplementation dose

claim_text: Periconceptional folic acid supplementation reduces neural tube defects.
population: people capable of pregnancy in the periconceptional period
applicability: folic acid form and periconceptional timing are constitutive
uncertainty: cannot be bound to current dish field until folate/folic-acid/DFE semantics are confirmed
prohibited_overclaims: a dish with FolicAcid field value prevents NTDs

claim_text: Dietary cholesterol cannot be interpreted as a simple stand-alone cardiovascular risk threshold; observational studies generally show no significant CVD association, while many interventions show higher intake can raise total or LDL cholesterol, and guidance emphasizes overall dietary patterns.
applicability: must consider saturated fat, food source and overall dietary pattern
uncertainty: direct CVD effect is difficult to isolate from correlated diet components
prohibited_overclaims: cholesterol mg alone labels a dish heart-healthy/unhealthy; universal numeric cholesterol cutoff

claim_text: For patients with gout, limiting purine intake is conditionally recommended; certainty of evidence for this lifestyle recommendation is low.
applicability: gout population only; lifestyle adjunct to clinical management
uncertainty: dietary changes often yield modest serum-urate changes
prohibited_overclaims: purine-rich dish is unhealthy for the general population; diet replaces urate-lowering therapy

claim_text: Higher purine intake is associated with increased gout-flare risk, with evidence suggesting animal-source purines may be more relevant than a simple total-purine quantity.
applicability: requires disease status and ideally purine source type
uncertainty: dietary studies are heterogeneous; serum-urate effects are inconsistent
prohibited_overclaims: all purines have identical effects; total purine mg alone predicts flare probability
